title: The missing minutes
bodyMd:
A fictional city compared two bus routes with the same average journey time. On one route, most trips took between twenty-eight and thirty-two minutes. On the other, trips ranged from eighteen to forty-two minutes. Passengers on the second route often left home much earlier than the average would suggest, because arriving late carried a greater cost than arriving early.

The transport office had previously advertised improvements only through reductions in average journey time. It began publishing a reliability measure as well. This did not make the mean useless: it remained relevant for comparing the total time spent travelling across many journeys. But the variation mattered to an individual deciding when to leave for a fixed appointment. A small improvement in the mean could be less valuable to that passenger than a substantial reduction in the chance of a very long delay.
